Stress And Economic Health

Didier Darcet

Gavekal-IS | 26 Nov 2026

Two patients lie in beds in the same hospital room. Both have suffered a comparable deterioration in their health. One recovers quickly, while the other faces a much longer and more uncertain road ahead. Why? The first was in good health before being struck by an external shock, such as a bicycle accident. The second, by contrast, was already weakened by a succession of chronic illnesses.In economics, as in medicine, the ability to withstand stress depends fundamentally on the condition of the system before the shock occurs. And, as we argue in this letter, the global economy today is in poor health.
